summary: REPAIR — public.public_get_quote_by_token(uuid) re-issued from its LIVE body to include 'onboarding_access_token' in the returned payload. Without it, every client who accepted a proposal was stuck permanently on 'Preparing your secure onboarding link…' and could never reach onboarding. Additive to the payload only: every existing key keeps its name, type and meaning, and no table, column, policy or trigger is touched.

problem.symptom: After accepting a proposal the client-facing page sits on 'Preparing your secure onboarding link…' indefinitely and the Continue Onboarding retry never resolves.
problem.root_cause: Confirmed live 2026-07-27, not inferred. (1) public_accept_quote_by_token (live 4199627dad4b3e8d9c9e90f5872d0e72) returns only {success, client_id, company_id, partnership_id} — it neither creates the onboarding application nor returns a token. (2) The application is created LAZILY by public_get_quote_by_token, which the client polls — but the live body (4e250dfdaccaa30a12e33f5b52cbd6cc) returned 'onboarding_application_id' with NO 'onboarding_access_token' key at all. (3) src/pages/PublicQuoteView.tsx deliberately refuses to navigate without BOTH values, because a tokenless /onboard/:id trips the strict lifecycle_require_onboarding_token guard and fails with a worse, cryptic error. So the client retried, never received a token, and stopped at the 'preparing' message.
problem.not_the_cause: The onboarding rows are healthy. The application created 2026-07-27T17:12:53Z (eb73d94d-d6a7-4c74-9fd5-50c22b30786b) carries a valid access_token and a 2026-10-25 expiry, so the column DEFAULT and trg_ensure_onboarding_access_token established by 20260722160000 are working. Only the read path was broken.
problem.drift: This is live-vs-git divergence, not a missing change: the repo's own definition (20260623215536) has returned onboarding_access_token since June, and nothing since redefines it. The live copy diverged. The repair is therefore based on the LIVE body, not re-pasted from git, so whatever else drifted in that function is preserved rather than silently reverted.

live_bodies_used.basis: Full body fetched via MCP catalog_functions(include_source: true) and reproduced verbatim except five documented changes: v_access_token declared; the existing-application lookup also selects access_token; the lazy INSERT also RETURNS access_token; a self-heal for any pre-trigger row still missing a token; and the new key in the returned payload.
Read only, NOT modified — fetched to establish that it neither creates the onboarding application nor returns a token, which is why the read path is the correct place to repair this.

expected_objects.object: public.public_get_quote_by_token(uuid) returns a payload containing onboarding_access_token
expected_objects.evidence: Applied in order and verified by the executor 2026-07-27: the function returns onboarding_access_token, and its def-hash moved from 4e250dfdaccaa30a12e33f5b52cbd6cc to aef93b68… (which also carries the annual-bucket change from 20260727170000, applied immediately after). NOT independently re-checked by Claude — the connector token had expired at the time of reporting; to be reconfirmed on the next connected session.
expected_objects.verify_via: catalog_functions(name_like: 'public_get_quote_by_token', include_source: true) -> def-hash CHANGED from 4e250dfdaccaa30a12e33f5b52cbd6cc; body contains "'onboarding_access_token', v_access_token" and RETURNING id, access_token. Then db_rpc public_get_quote_by_token with the live acceptance token for quote 753529f8-a903-4c84-b397-0a5ed0f3e82d and confirm the payload now carries a non-null onboarding_access_token alongside the existing onboarding_application_id.

expected_objects.object: public_get_quote_by_token returns onboarding_access_token = null for a quote that is not accepted
expected_objects.verify_via: db_rpc public_get_quote_by_token with the acceptance token of a DRAFT or SENT quote and confirm onboarding_access_token is null while the rest of the payload is unchanged. Holding a proposal link must not expose the onboarding secret before acceptance.

expected_objects.object: The already-accepted proposal reaches onboarding without any data repair
expected_objects.verify_via: Reopen the client proposal link for quote 753529f8. It must now navigate to onboarding instead of showing 'Preparing your secure onboarding link…'. Application eb73d94d already holds a valid token, so no backfill is required — the read path alone was broken.

rollback.assessment: Forward-only. The previous behaviour can be restored from the recorded live body 4e250dfdaccaa30a12e33f5b52cbd6cc, but doing so reinstates the defect that blocks every client from onboarding.
rollback.data_risk: None on apply. At runtime the only write added is the self-heal, which sets access_token on rows where it is NULL or empty — it can never overwrite an existing token.

steps: Apply migration 20260727160000_quote_token_returns_onboarding_token.sql via the Lovable migration flow.
Confirm the card returns green AND a row exists in supabase_migrations.schema_migrations (verify against LIVE, not just Test).
Reopen the accepted proposal's client link and confirm it now reaches onboarding.
After apply: refresh docs/audits/unapplied-migrations-baseline.json with the new applied version so the drift guard stays green.
Notify Claude to run the expected-object verification and complete this receipt (move out of pending/).

post_apply_followups: public_accept_quote_by_token still returns neither the onboarding id nor its token, leaving the client dependent on a poll-and-retry loop against the read path — and leaving a gap where a client who accepts and closes the tab has no onboarding application until someone reopens the quote link. Creating the application AT acceptance and returning both keys (including on the 'replay' return) closes both. Worth doing, but as its own increment with its own receipt: that function is ~250 lines, creates clients/companies/partnerships and materialises jobs on the legacy path, so it must not be re-issued as a side effect of a read-path repair.

NOT adopted, deliberately: rotating an expired access_token on read. It would smooth the returning-client experience, but auto-renewing a secret on demand defeats the point of access_token_expires_at — anyone holding the proposal link could refresh the onboarding token indefinitely. If a returning client should get a fresh link, that is a product decision about re-issuing it through a deliberate, audited action, not a silent side effect of a read.

This drift was invisible until a client hit it. The function-level equivalent of the migration receipt gate — comparing live def-hashes for the public onboarding RPCs against the hashes this repo last shipped — would have caught it. Candidate for the next governance increment.
